Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma, production marketing site). Work in an isolated git worktree — `git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wip-location-pages -b feature/expand-location-pages` from /opt/nxeon — do NOT touch the live tree or merge into main. Symlink node_modules/.env; never `git add -A` in a worktree.

## Context

Nxeon already has a real, data-driven programmatic SEO system for location+service landing pages: `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` defines `LocationDef`/`ServiceDef` types and a combo matrix, rendered by the single dynamic route `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx` (e.g. `/singapore-vps-hosting`, `/frankfurt-game-server-hosting`). Currently 11 locations (Singapore, London, Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Paris, New York, Toronto, Los Angeles, Sydney, Tokyo, Mumbai) × 4 services (vps-hosting, game-server-hosting, web-hosting, dedicated-server-hosting). Read both files fully before doing anything.

Real Search Console data pulled today shows these pages ARE being indexed but ranking very poorly for commercial intent terms (e.g. "cheap vps singapore" at position 79, "frankfurt vps" at position 73) — this is attributed to the domain being ~5 weeks old with no backlink authority yet, not a content problem. The owner wants MORE of these pages built regardless, as a long-term SEO investment, plus they specifically mentioned wanting American locations (e.g. "America VPS") and "other types as well" (new service categories beyond the current 4).

## CRITICAL — honesty constraint, read this before adding anything

**Do not fabricate infrastructure claims.** Before adding ANY new location, verify what's actually true about Nxeon's real infrastructure footprint. Read `lib/ovh.ts`, `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`, and any node/region config (`prisma/schema.prisma`'s `Node` model, `lib/node-capacity.ts`) to understand where servers are ACTUALLY provisioned (this session's context: the platform runs on Proxmox nodes behind OVH's network — check whether there is genuinely more than one physical PoP/region, or whether "location" pages are currently more about network routing/latency claims than literal separate datacenters). Read the EXISTING location pages' actual copy (e.g. `/singapore-vps-hosting`) to see exactly what claim pattern they already use (e.g. do they say "hosted in Singapore" — a literal claim — or "optimized for Singapore" / "low-latency access from Singapore" — a routing/latency claim). Whatever the existing honest pattern is, follow the SAME level of honesty for every new location — if you cannot verify a location has genuine infrastructure backing it, either don't add it, or write its copy using the same non-literal "optimized for / low-latency access" framing the existing pages already establish (do not invent a stronger claim than what's already true elsewhere on the site). If you're at all unsure whether a location can be honestly added, list it in your report as a question for the owner rather than guessing.

## What to build

1. **New locations** — expand toward genuinely high-value, high-search-volume VPS/hosting markets not yet covered (e.g. Dallas, Miami, Chicago, Seoul, Hong Kong, Dubai, São Paulo, Mumbai is already covered — pick ones with real commercial search demand, you can use WebSearch to sanity-check search interest isn't negligible for a candidate before adding it). Subject to the honesty constraint above.

2. **New service/type variants** beyond the current 4 — real, searched commercial terms relevant to VPS/game/hosting customers. Consider (verify search relevance yourself, don't just take my suggestions blindly): "minecraft-hosting" (game-specific, high search volume — check if this overlaps/conflicts with the EXISTING dedicated `/minecraft-server-hosting` type pages elsewhere in the codebase first, avoid creating a duplicate/competing page), "cheap-vps-hosting" per-location (there's already a global `/cheap-vps-hosting` — decide if a per-location variant adds value or cannibalizes it), "discord-bot-hosting", "forex-vps-hosting" (a real, specific, high-intent VPS use case — low-latency trading VPS is a known lucrative niche), "reseller-hosting". Use your judgment on which 2-4 new types are worth adding — don't just add all of them reflexively; each one needs genuinely differentiated content, not a template with find/replace.

3. **Avoid thin/duplicate content** — Google penalizes near-identical pages differing only in a swapped city/service name. Read how the existing template already handles differentiation (per-location latency numbers, per-service feature emphasis, etc.) and make sure new combos genuinely add unique value per page, not just a different H1.

4. **Update the sitemap** (`app/sitemap.ts`, already confirmed to include the location-landing combos — verify new combos are automatically picked up by whatever mechanism already includes the current ones, or wire it in if it's not automatic).

## What NOT to do

- Do not touch the custom-server-plans, Namecheap/registrar, PayPal, or board-processing work — separate agents in parallel, unrelated worktrees.
- Do not touch the blog post content/seed data.
- Do not deploy to staging/production — I review and ship.

## Verification

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. `npm test` — no new failures beyond the current 34 pre-existing baseline (pricing/proration/auth-related, unrelated to marketing pages).
3. Spot-check a few of the new combo pages render correctly (build locally or use whatever preview mechanism this repo's past sessions used — check for an existing dev-server pattern).

## Report format

List every new location added with your honesty-verification reasoning for each, every new service type added with your relevance reasoning, any location you considered but declined to add (and why), files created/modified, verification results, worktree path/branch name.

### 7 new locations added (all `presence: "market"` or `"network"` — never `"datacenter"`)

Confirmed via `prisma/schema.prisma`'s single `Node` model, `lib/ovh.ts`, and the file's own header comment that Nxeon has exactly one real datacenter (Singapore); every other location in the existing matrix already uses the "audience/market" framing with an honest FAQ answer ("our production platform runs from a Singapore datacenter today..."). - **Dallas** — `network` — real Infomart/Equinix carrier-hotel hub; owner explicitly wanted more American locations; competitor VPS providers (HostZealot, VPSServer.com) already sell "Dallas VPS," confirming commercial intent.
- **Miami** — `network` — NAP of the Americas, genuine LatAm/Caribbean gateway; fills the US-Southeast/LatAm gap.

- **Seoul** — `network` — KINX + Korea's outsized competitive-gaming market (relevant to the existing game-server-hosting combo).
- **Dubai** — `market` — Gulf's main subsea cable landing point; underserved Middle-East region.
- **São Paulo** — `network` — IX.br, world's largest exchange by connected networks; Brazil/LatAm demand confirmed in data-center market research.

**Considered and declined:** none outright rejected on honesty grounds — all 7 passed the same "market/network, no datacenter claim" bar already established by the existing 10 non-Singapore locations. I did not add a generic "USA" or "America VPS" catch-all page since the existing pattern is city-specific with real hub facts (New York/Toronto/LA already cover US East/Canada/US West); a generic country-wide page would be thinner content than the city pages and risked duplicating them, so I expanded US coverage with real cities (Dallas, Miami, Chicago) instead.
